name: Passerellidae
description: Passerellidae, the New World sparrows, are a large and diverse family of passerine birds found primarily in the Americas. They are seed-eating birds with conical bills, often with streaked brown plumage and melodious songs.

children.name: Zonotrichia
children.description: A genus of large, handsome sparrows with distinctive crown patterns, found across North America.

children.name: Zonotrichia leucophrys
children.description: The white-crowned sparrow is a species of passerine bird native to North America. A medium-sized member of the New World sparrow family, this species is marked by a grey face and black and white streaking on the upper head. It breeds in brushy areas in the taiga and tundra of the northernmost parts of the continent and in the Rocky Mountains and Pacific coast.

children.name: Zonotrichia albicollis
children.description: The white-throated sparrow (Zonotrichia albicollis) is a passerine bird of the New World sparrow family Passerellidae. It breeds in northern North America and winters in the southern United States.

children.name: Zonotrichia atricapilla
children.description: The golden-crowned sparrow (Zonotrichia atricapilla) is a large New World sparrow found in the western part of North America.

children.name: Zonotrichia querula
children.description: Harris's sparrow (Zonotrichia querula) is a large sparrow. Their breeding habitat is the north part of central Canada (primarily the Northwest Territories and Nunavut, ranging slightly into northern Manitoba and Saskatchewan), making it Canada's only endemic breeding bird. In the winter they migrate to the Great Plains states of the United States, from southern South Dakota to central Texas. The common name of this species commemorates the American amateur ornithologist Edward Harris.

children.name: Zonotrichia spathz
children.description: This newly described species, Zonotrichia spathz, is a small passerine bird known for its distinct song and preference for forested habitats.

children.name: Melospiza
children.description: A genus of medium-sized, heavily streaked sparrows found across North America.

children.name: Melospiza melodia
children.description: The song sparrow is a medium-sized New World sparrow. Among the native sparrows in North America, it is easily one of the most abundant, variable, and adaptable species.

children.name: Melospiza lincolnii
children.description: Lincoln's sparrow (Melospiza lincolnii) is a small sparrow native to North America. It is a less common passerine bird that often stays hidden under thick ground cover, but can be distinguished by its sweet, wrenlike song. Lincoln's sparrow is one of three species in the genus Melospiza which also includes the song sparrow (M. Melodia) and the swamp sparrow (M. Georgiana). It lives in well-covered brushy habitats, often near water. This bird is poorly documented because of its secretive nature and breeding habits solely in boreal regions.

children.name: Melospiza georgiana
children.description: The swamp sparrow (Melospiza georgiana) is a medium-sized New World sparrow related to the song sparrow.

children.name: Centronyx
children.description: A small genus of grassland sparrows formerly placed in Ammodramus, found in the prairies of North America.

children.name: Centronyx bairdii
children.description: Baird's sparrow (Centronyx bairdii) is a species of North American birds in the family Passerellidae of order Passeriformes. It is a migratory bird native to the United States, Canada, and Mexico.

children.name: Centronyx henslowii
children.description: Henslow's sparrow (Centronyx henslowii) is a North American passerine bird in the family Passerellidae. It was named by John James Audubon in honor of John Stevens Henslow. It was originally classified in the genus Emberiza and called Henslow's bunting.

children.name: Spizella
children.description: A genus of small, slender sparrows with rufous crowns and plain underparts, found across North America.

children.name: Spizella passerina
children.description: The chipping sparrow (Spizella passerina) is a species of New World sparrow, a passerine bird in the family Passerellidae.

children.name: Spizella pallida
children.description:
The clay-colored sparrow or clay-coloured sparrow (Spizella pallida) is a small New World sparrow of North America.
Adults have light brown upperparts and pale underparts, with darker streaks on the back. They have a pale crown stripe on a dark brown crown, a white line over the eyes, a dark line through the eyes, a light brown cheek patch and brown wings with wing bars. The short bill is pale with a dark tip and the back of the neck is grey; they have a long tail. Non-breeding adults and immature resemble chipping sparrows and Brewer's sparrows; they often form flocks with these birds outside the nesting season.

children.name: Spizella breweri
children.description: Brewer's sparrow (Spizella breweri) is a small, slim species of American sparrow in the family Passerellidae. This bird was named after the ornithologist Thomas Mayo Brewer.

children.name: Spizella pusilla
children.description: The field sparrow is a small New World sparrow in the family Passerellidae. It is about 140 mm (6 in) long and weighs about 12.5 g (0.4 oz). The head is grey with a rust-coloured crown, white eye-ring and pink bill.

children.name: Spizella atrogularis
children.description:
The black-chinned sparrow (Spizella atrogularis) is a small bird in the genus Spizella, in the New World sparrow family Passerellidae. It is found in the southwestern United States and throughout much of Mexico north of the Isthmus of Tehuantepec; most populations in the US migrate south after breeding while those in Mexico are. It is a slim, long-tailed bird, primarily gray with a reddish-brown back streaked with black, brown wings and tail, a pink beak, and brownish legs and feet. In the breeding season, the male shows black on his throat, chin, and the front of his face. Females, youngsters and nonbreeding males show little or no black in these areas. An unobtrusive bird, it spends much of its time foraging slowly along the ground, either alone or in small groups, sometimes mixing with other Spizella species. It is an omnivore, feeding primarily on seeds during the winter and insects during the summer. It builds a cup-shaped nest of grasses, rootlets, or plant fibers, into which the female lays 2–5 pale blue eggs. The female does most or all of the egg incubation, but both parents feed the hatched nestlings.
The species was first described by Jean Louis Cabanis in 1851. Four subspecies have been identified: one breeds only in the US, one only in Mexico, and the other two breed in both countries. Most northern populations move south—primarily into Mexico—for the winter. Because of its apparently large population size and very large range, it is considered to be a species of least concern. However, increasing global temperatures could have a significantly negative impact on its numbers.

children.name: Spizella wortheni
children.description: Worthen's sparrow (Spizella wortheni) is a species of American sparrow that is endemic to northeastern Mexico. It was first described by Robert Ridgway in 1884 and named for the American naturalist Charles K. Worthen. This small bird has been listed as endangered by the IUCN since 1994.

children.name: Junco
children.description: A genus of sparrows with grey or brown plumage and white outer tail feathers, found across North America.

children.name: Junco hyemalis
children.description: The dark-eyed junco (Junco hyemalis) is a species of junco, a group of small, grayish New World sparrows. The species is common across much of temperate North America and in summer it ranges far into the Arctic. It is a variable species, much like the related fox sparrow (Passerella iliaca), and its systematics are still not completely resolved.

children.name: Junco phaeonotus
children.description: The yellow-eyed junco (Junco phaeonotus) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found from the southwestern United States to Guatemala.

children.name: Junco vulcani
children.description: The volcano junco (Junco vulcani) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.

children.name: Junco insularis
children.description: The Guadalupe junco (Junco insularis) is a small bird in the New World sparrow family that is endemic to Guadalupe Island off the western coast of Baja California, Mexico.

children.name: Passerella
children.description: A genus of large, heavily built sparrows with variable rufous and grey plumage.

children.name: Passerella iliaca
children.description: The fox sparrow (Passerella iliaca) is a large New World sparrow.

children.name: Passerella unalaschcensis
children.description: The sooty fox sparrow (Passerella (iliaca) unalaschcensis) contains the darkest-colored taxa in the genus Passerella. It is currently classified as a "subspecies group" within the fox sparrow pending wider-spread acceptance of species status. It has long been suspected to be a separate evolutionary lineage due to morphological distinctness (Swarth 1920), and this is confirmed by analysis of mtDNA sequence and haplotype data (Zink 1994, Zink & Kessen 1999, Zink & Weckstein 2003). This group appears to be most closely related to the thick-billed and/or slate-colored fox sparrows (Zink 1996, Zink & Weckstein 2003).

children.name: Passerella schistacea
children.description:
The slate-colored fox sparrow (Passerella (iliaca) schistacea) group comprises the Rocky Mountain taxa in the genus Passerella. It is currently classified as a "subspecies group" within the fox sparrows pending a more-thorough genetic assay of all forms.
It has long been suspected to be a separate evolutionary lineage due to morphological distinctness (Swarth 1920). More recently, it has been split into the present clade and the thick-billed fox sparrow. These have quite similar plumage, but can be readily distinguished according to mtDNA sequence and haplotype data (Zink 1994). However, these results were considered tentative (Rising & Beadle 1996) until more molecular data and apparent lack of wide-ranging hybridization coupled with ecological differences and adaptations led to confirmation of their distinctiveness (Zink & Kessen 1999); this group appears to be most closely related to the red fox sparrows (Zink & Weckstein 2003 contra Zink 1996), judging from biogeography.

children.name: Passerella megarhyncha
children.description:
The thick-billed fox sparrow (Passerella (iliaca) megarhyncha) group comprises the peculiarly large-billed Sierra Nevadan taxa in the genus Passerella. It is currently classified as a "subspecies group" within the fox sparrow, pending wider-spread acceptance of its species status.
These birds were long considered members of the slate-colored fox sparrow group due to morphological characteristics (Swarth 1920), but according to mtDNA cytochrome b sequence and haplotype data (Zink 1994), it forms a recognizable clade. Research on suspected (Rising & Beadle 1996) hybridization and considering additional DNA sequence data led to confirmation of their distinctiveness (Zink & Kessen 1999); this group appears to be most closely related to the sooty and/or slate-colored fox sparrows. (Zink 1996, Zink & Weckstein 2003)

children.name: Peucaea
children.description: A genus of medium-sized sparrows with stout bills and often rufous wings, found in arid and semi-arid habitats from the southern United States through Mexico and Central America.

children.name: Peucaea botterii
children.description: Botteri's sparrow (Peucaea botterii) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found from the southwestern United States to Costa Rica.

children.name: Peucaea cassinii
children.description:
Cassin's sparrow (Peucaea cassinii) is a medium-sized sparrow.
This passerine bird's range is from western Nebraska to north-central Mexico.

children.name: Peucaea aestivalis
children.description:
Bachman's sparrow (Peucaea aestivalis), also known as the pinewoods sparrow or oakwoods sparrow, is a small American sparrow that is endemic to the southeastern United States. This species was named in honor of Reverend John Bachman.
Adults have rufous brown upperparts and crown with gray and black streaking on the nape, back and primaries. The face is gray with a rufous brown eyestripe. It has a buff colored breast and whitish belly. These are mid-sized New World sparrows, measuring and.

children.name: Peucaea carpalis
children.description: The rufous-winged sparrow (Peucaea carpalis) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in Mexico and the United States.

children.name: Peucaea ruficauda
children.description: The stripe-headed sparrow (Peucaea ruficauda) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found from Mexico to Costa Rica.

children.name: Peucaea humeralis
children.description: The black-chested sparrow (Peucaea humeralis) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is endemic to Mexico.

children.name: Artemisiospiza
children.description: A genus of pale, desert-dwelling sparrows formerly placed in Amphispiza, found in sagebrush and saltbush habitats of western North America.

children.name: Artemisiospiza belli
children.description: Bell's sparrow (Artemisiospiza belli) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in Mexico and the United States.

children.name: Artemisiospiza nevadensis
children.description: The sagebrush sparrow (Artemisiospiza nevadensis) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.

children.name: Pooecetes
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Vesper Sparrow, a long-bodied sparrow of open grasslands and fields across North America.

children.name: Pooecetes gramineus
children.description: The vesper sparrow (Pooecetes gramineus) is a medium-sized New World sparrow.

children.name: Passerculus
children.description: A widespread genus of small, streaked sparrows found in grasslands across North America. The Savannah Sparrow complex shows remarkable variation across subspecies, some of which were once considered separate species.

children.name: Passerculus sandwichensis
children.description: The Savannah sparrow is a small New World sparrow that is the only member of the genus Passerculus. It is a widespread and abundant species that occupies open grassland habitats in North America.

children.name: Ammodramus
children.description: A genus of chunky, short-tailed sparrows adapted to dense grasslands, found across North America. They are notoriously secretive and are more often heard than seen, but their insect-like songs carry far across open fields.

children.name: Ammodramus savannarum
children.description: The grasshopper sparrow (Ammodramus savannarum) is a small New World sparrow.

children.name: Ammodramus humeralis
children.description: The grassland sparrow (Ammodramus humeralis) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae.

children.name: Ammospiza
children.description: A genus of sparrows specialised for life in coastal salt marshes, tidal creeks, and brackish wetlands along the coasts of North America. They have distinctive, rather flat heads and stout bills adapted for a diet of small crustaceans and insects in addition to seeds.

children.name: Ammospiza nelsoni
children.description: Nelson's sparrow (Ammospiza nelsoni) is a small New World sparrow.

children.name: Ammospiza maritima
children.description: The seaside sparrow (Ammospiza maritima) is a species of American sparrow.

children.name: Ammospiza caudacuta
children.description: The saltmarsh sparrow (Ammospiza caudacuta) is a small New World sparrow found in salt marshes along the Atlantic coast of the United States.

children.name: Ammospiza leconteii
children.description: LeConte's sparrow (Ammospiza leconteii), also known as LeConte's bunting, is one of the smallest New World sparrow species in North America.

children.name: Pipilo
children.description: A genus of large, handsome sparrows known as towhees, characterised by long tails, stout bills, and striking plumage patterns. They are primarily ground-foraging birds that scratch loudly through leaf litter with both feet in a backwards hop.

children.name: Pipilo chlorurus
children.description: The green-tailed towhee (Pipilo chlorurus) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in the western United States and much of Mexico.

children.name: Pipilo maculatus
children.description: The spotted towhee (Pipilo maculatus) is a large New World sparrow.

children.name: Pipilo erythrophthalmus
children.description: The eastern towhee, also known as chewink, joree, or joree bird, is a large New World sparrow. The taxonomy of the towhees has been under debate in recent decades, and formerly this bird and the spotted towhee were considered a single species, the rufous-sided towhee.

children.name: Pipilo ocai
children.description: The collared towhee (Pipilo ocai) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.

children.name: Melozone
children.description: A genus of medium-sized sparrows with often plain brown or strikingly patterned plumage, found from the southwestern United States through Mexico to Central America.

children.name: Melozone crissalis
children.description: The California towhee (Melozone crissalis) is a bird of the family Passerellidae, native to the coastal regions of western Oregon and California in the United States and Baja California and Baja California Sur in Mexico.

children.name: Melozone fusca
children.description: The canyon towhee (Melozone fusca) is a bird of the family Passerellidae.

children.name: Melozone aberti
children.description: Abert's towhee (Melozone aberti) is a bird of the family Passerellidae, native to a small range in southwestern North America, generally the lower Colorado River and Gila River watersheds, nearly endemic to Arizona, but also present in small parts of California, Nevada, Utah, New Mexico, and Sonora in Mexico. The name of this bird commemorates the American ornithologist James William Abert.

children.name: Melozone biarcuata
children.description: Prevost's ground sparrow (Melozone biarcuata), also known as the white-faced ground sparrow, is an American sparrow.

children.name: Melozone leucotis
children.description: The white-eared ground sparrow (Melozone leucotis) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in Costa Rica, Honduras, and Nicaragua.

children.name: Melozone kieneri
children.description: The rusty-crowned ground sparrow (Melozone kieneri) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is endemic to Mexico.

children.name: Aimophila
children.description: A genus of medium-sized sparrows with long tails and rusty crowns, found in arid and semi-arid scrublands from the southwestern United States through Mexico and Central America.

children.name: Aimophila ruficeps
children.description:
The rufous-crowned sparrow (Aimophila ruficeps) is a small American sparrow. This passerine is primarily found across the Southwestern United States and much of the interior of Mexico, south to the transverse mountain range, and to the Pacific coast to the southwest of the transverse range. Its distribution is patchy, with populations often being isolated from each other. Twelve subspecies are generally recognized, though up to eighteen have been suggested. This bird has a brown back with darker streaks and gray underparts. The crown is rufous, and the face and supercilium are gray with a brown or rufous streak extending from each eye and a thick black malar streak.
These sparrows feed primarily on seeds in the winter and insects in the spring and summer. The birds are often territorial, with males guarding their territory through song and displays. Flight is awkward for this species, which prefers to hop along the ground for locomotion. They are monogamous and breed during spring. Two to five eggs are laid in the bird's nest, which is cup-shaped and well hidden. Adult sparrows are preyed upon by house cats and small raptors, while young may be taken by a range of mammals and reptiles. They have been known to live for up to three years, two months. Although the species has been classified as least concern, or unthreatened with extinction, some subspecies are threatened by habitat destruction and one may be extinct.

children.name: Aimophila notosticta
children.description: The Oaxaca sparrow (Aimophila notosticta) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.

children.name: Amphispiza
children.description: A small genus of pale, desert-dwelling sparrows with striking facial patterns. They are well adapted to arid environments and are characteristic birds of the deserts and dry scrublands of western North America.

children.name: Amphispiza bilineata
children.description: The black-throated sparrow (Amphispiza bilineata) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in Mexico and the United States.

children.name: Chondestes
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Lark Sparrow, one of the most distinctive North American sparrows with a striking facial pattern of chestnut, black, and white. It has a long, rounded tail and a stout seed-cracking bill.

children.name: Chondestes grammacus
children.description: The lark sparrow (Chondestes grammacus) is a fairly large New World sparrow.

children.name: Rhynchospiza
children.description: A small genus of sparrows found in arid and semi-arid scrublands of western South America. They were formerly included in Aimophila and have stout, conical bills adapted for seed-cracking.

children.name: Rhynchospiza stolzmanni
children.description: }} The Tumbes sparrow (Rhynchospiza stolzmanni) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae found in Ecuador and Peru.

children.name: Rhynchospiza strigiceps
children.description: | range_map = Rhynchospiza strigiceps map.svg.

children.name: Pezopetes
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Large-footed Finch, a large, terrestrial sparrow of montane forests in Central America. It is named for its unusually large, powerful feet adapted for scratching through leaf litter.

children.name: Pezopetes capitalis
children.description: The large-footed finch (Pezopetes capitalis) is a species of bird that despite its name is in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

children.name: Torreornis
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Zapata Sparrow, a secretive, ground-dwelling sparrow endemic to Cuba and one of the most restricted-range passerines in the Americas.

children.name: Torreornis inexpectata
children.description: | range_map = Torreornis inexpectata map.svg }}.

children.name: Xenospiza
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Sierra Madre Sparrow, a highly range-restricted species endemic to highland grasslands of Mexico. It is threatened by habitat loss and agricultural intensification.

children.name: Xenospiza baileyi
children.description: The Sierra Madre sparrow (Xenospiza baileyi), also known as Bailey's sparrow, is an endangered, range-restricted, enigmatic American sparrow. It is endemic to Mexico and is threatened with extinction through habitat loss.

children.name: Arremonops
children.description: A genus of medium-sized, olive-backed sparrows with striped heads, found from southern Texas through Mexico and Central America to northern South America.

children.name: Arremonops rufivirgatus
children.description: The olive sparrow (Arremonops rufivirgatus) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.

children.name: Arremonops chloronotus
children.description: The green-backed sparrow (Arremonops chloronotus) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in Belize, Guatemala, Honduras, and Mexico.

children.name: Arremonops conirostris
children.description: The black-striped sparrow (Arremonops conirostris) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found from Honduras south to Ecuador and Brazil. There are also unconfirmed reports in Peru.

children.name: Arremon
children.description: A genus of sparrows and brush finches with striking black, white, and olive plumage patterns, found from Mexico through Central and South America. They inhabit forest undergrowth and are often more easily heard than seen.

children.name: Arremon aurantiirostris
children.description: The orange-billed sparrow (Arremon aurantiirostris) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found from Mexico to Peru.

children.name: Arremon assimilis
children.description: The grey-browed brushfinch (Arremon assimilis) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru and Venezuela.

children.name: Arremon brunneinucha
children.description: The chestnut-capped brushfinch (Arremon brunneinucha) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found from Mexico to Peru.

children.name: Arremon crassirostris
children.description: The sooty-faced finch (Arremon crassirostris) is a species of bird in the family Emberizidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, and Panama.

children.name: Arremon flavirostris
children.description: The saffron-billed sparrow (Arremon flavirostris) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, and Paraguay.

children.name: Arremon semitorquatus
children.description: The half-collared sparrow (Arremon semitorquatus) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is endemic to Brazil.

children.name: Arremon franciscanus
children.description: The Sao Francisco sparrow (Arremon franciscanus) is a Near Threatened species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is endemic to Brazil.

children.name: Arremon castaneiceps
children.description: }} The olive finch (Arremon castaneiceps) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae.

children.name: Arremon laniirostris
children.description: A dull olive-brown brush finch with a grey head, pale throat, and a stout black bill. It ranges from Costa Rica through Central America to western Ecuador in humid lowland and premontane forests.

children.name: Arremon schlegeli
children.description: The Golden-winged sparrow (Arremon schlegeli) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae that can found in Colombia and Venezuela. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry forests and subtropical or tropical dry shrubland.

children.name: Atlapetes
children.description: A large genus of colorful brush finches with rufous, yellow, and olive plumage, found in montane forests and scrublands of Central and South America. They are active, often conspicuous birds that forage in pairs or small groups.

children.name: Atlapetes latinuchus
children.description: The yellow-breasted brushfinch (Atlapetes latinuchus) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru..

children.name: Atlapetes leucopterus
children.description: The white-winged brushfinch (Atlapetes leucopterus) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

children.name: Atlapetes pallidinucha
children.description: The pale-naped brushfinch (Atlapetes pallidinucha) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela.

children.name: Atlapetes semirufus
children.description: The ochre-breasted brushfinch (Atlapetes semirufus) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae. It is endemic to the northern Andes, occurring in Colombia and Venezuela. In Colombia, it inhabits elevations of 1,600–3,500 meters, while in Venezuela it is found between 600–2,700 meters. The species is present in several national parks and is not currently considered to face immediate conservation threats. Although relatively common, its breeding biology and life history remain poorly understood, and the population is believed to be in decline.

children.name: Atlapetes melanocephalus
children.description: The Santa Marta brushfinch (Atlapetes melanocephalus) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is endemic to the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta in northern Colombia.

children.name: Atlapetes pileatus
children.description: The rufous-capped brushfinch (Atlapetes pileatus) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is endemic to Mexico.

children.name: Atlapetes albinucha
children.description: The white-naped brushfinch (Atlapetes albinucha), also known as the yellow-throated brushfinch, is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found from Mexico to Ecuador.

children.name: Atlapetes gutturalis
children.description: The white-naped brushfinch (Atlapetes albinucha), also known as the yellow-throated brushfinch, is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found from Mexico to Ecuador.

children.name: Atlapetes personatus
children.description: The tepui brushfinch (Atlapetes personatus) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.

children.name: Atlapetes seebohmi
children.description: The bay-crowned brushfinch (Atlapetes seebohmi) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in Ecuador and Peru.

children.name: Atlapetes nationi
children.description: The rusty-bellied brushfinch (Atlapetes nationi) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is endemic to Peru.

children.name: Atlapetes canigenis
children.description: The Cuzco brushfinch (Atlapetes canigenis), also known as the grey brushfinch or sooty brushfinch, is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae.

children.name: Atlapetes schistaceus
children.description: The slaty brushfinch or northern slaty brushfinch (Atlapetes schistaceus) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.

children.name: Atlapetes rufigenis
children.description: The rufous-eared brushfinch (Atlapetes rufigenis) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is endemic to Peru.

children.name: Atlapetes citrinellus
children.description: The yellow-striped brushfinch (Atlapetes citrinellus) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is endemic to Argentina.

children.name: Atlapetes leucopis
children.description: The white-rimmed brushfinch (Atlapetes leucopis) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

children.name: Atlapetes tricolor
children.description: The tricolored brushfinch or golden-crowned brushfinch (Atlapetes tricolor) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows.

children.name: Atlapetes flaviceps
children.description:
The yellow-headed brushfinch (Atlapetes flaviceps) is a Near Threatened species of bird in the American sparrow family, Passerellidae. It is endemic to Colombia. The common name is a semi-literal translation of the scientific name, with Atlapetes referring to the brushfinch genus, and flaviceps meaning "yellow-headed".
This species has a yellow to dark olive head. The throat, chin, malar streak, lores, eye-ring, and ear patch are bright yellow in any case. The rest of the plumage is yellow with dark olive upperparts, wing and tail. The variation in the head color is not well explained, but it is likely that the olive-headed individuals are females and/or immature birds.

children.name: Atlapetes fuscoolivaceus
children.description: The dusky-headed brushfinch (Atlapetes fuscoolivaceus) is a Near Threatened species of bird in the family Emberizidae, the New World sparrows. It is endemic to Colombia.

children.name: Atlapetes nigrifrons
children.description: The black-fronted brushfinch (Atlapetes nigrifrons) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in Colombia and Venezuela.

children.name: Chlorospingus
children.description: A genus of small, olive-and-yellow birds formerly placed in the tanager family but now considered New World sparrows. They are active, social birds of montane forests from Mexico to South America.

children.name: Chlorospingus flavopectus
children.description: The common chlorospingus (Chlorospingus flavopectus), also referred to as common bush tanager, is a small passerine bird. It is a resident breeder in the highlands from central Mexico south to Bolivia and northwest Argentina. C. Flavopectus in the loose sense is a notorious cryptic species complex, and several of the up to 25 subspecies recognized in recent times are likely to be distinct species. Some populations in fact appear to be more distinct than several other members of Chlorospingus.

children.name: Chlorospingus semifuscus
children.description: The dusky chlorospingus or dusky bush tanager (Chlorospingus semifuscus) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

children.name: Chlorospingus flavovirens
children.description:
The yellow-green tanager (Bangsia flavovirens) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It was formerly known as the yellow-green bush tanager or yellow-green chlorospingus as it used to be placed in the genus Chlorospingus with other bush tanagers. Chlorospingus as a whole was formerly placed in the tanager family Thraupidae, but was transferred to the New World sparrows when genetic analysis of two Chlorospingus species revealed they were embedded within the latter family. However, more recently, molecular analysis of additional Chlorospingus species found that the yellow-green tanager is not a member of Chlorospingus (or any other New World sparrow) but a true tanager after all, most closely related to the blue-and-gold tanager, so the species was returned to Thraupidae and placed in the genus Bangsia.
The yellow-green tanager is found in Colombia and Ecuador. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest. It is threatened by habitat loss.

children.name: Chlorospingus canigularis
children.description: The ashy-throated chlorospingus (Chlorospingus canigularis) or ashy-throated bush tanager, is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Panama, Peru, and Venezuela.

children.name: Chlorospingus parvirostris
children.description: The yellow-whiskered chlorospingus (Chlorospingus parvirostris) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru. Some taxonomic systems call it the short-billed chlorospingus.

children.name: Chlorospingus pileatus
children.description: The sooty-capped chlorospingus (Chlorospingus pileatus) or sooty-capped bush tanager, is a small passerine bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in Costa Rica and Panama.

children.name: Chlorospingus flavigularis
children.description: The yellow-throated chlorospingus or yellow-throated bush tanager (Chlorospingus flavigularis) is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, Panama, and Peru.

children.name: Chlorospingus tacarcunae
children.description: The Tacarcuna chlorospingus (Chlorospingus tacarcunae) or Tacarcuna bush tanager is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is found in Colombia and Panama.

children.name: Chlorospingus inornatus
children.description: The Pirre chlorospingus (Chlorospingus inornatus) or Pirre bush tanager is a species of bird in the family Passerellidae, the New World sparrows. It is endemic to Panama.

children.name: Chlorospingus novaeguineae
children.description: A bush tanager with olive-green upperparts, bright yellow underparts, and a blackish crown. It is found in the Darien highlands of Panama and Colombia.

children.name: Oreothraupis
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Tanager Finch, a distinctive bird with a thick bill and striking black-and-white head pattern. It was once considered a tanager but is now placed in the New World sparrow family.

children.name: Pipilopsis
children.description: A small genus of sparrows with boldly striped heads, found in the Andes of South America.

children.name: Pipilopsis leucoptera
children.description: A sparrow with a black-and-white striped head, olive-brown upperparts, and white underparts. It is found in the Andes of Peru and Bolivia.

children.name: Pipilopsis boliviana
children.description: A sparrow with a striped head, brown upperparts, and pale underparts. It is endemic to the highlands of Bolivia.

children.name: Haplospiza
children.description: A small genus of finches with uniformly dark grey or slaty plumage in males, found in Central and South America. They inhabit forest edges and clearings, feeding on grass seeds and bamboo seeds.

children.name: Haplospiza unicolor
children.description: The uniform finch (Haplospiza unicolor) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae.

children.name: Haplospiza rustica
children.description: The slaty finch (Haplospiza rustica) is a bird species in the family Thraupidae (formerly in Emberizidae).

children.name: Acanthidops
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Peg-billed Finch, a distinctive bird of high-altitude scrub in Central America. It has a uniquely shaped, upturned bill adapted for extracting seeds from bamboo flowers.

children.name: Acanthidops barbatus
children.description: A small finch with a distinctive pale, upturned bill, grey upperparts, white underparts, and white outer tail feathers. It is found in highland scrub and bamboo thickets of Costa Rica and western Panama.

children.name: Spizellopsis
children.description: A genus of finches with streaked brown plumage, found in grasslands and open habitats of South America.

children.name: Spizellopsis brunneiventris
children.description: A finch with streaked brown upperparts, brownish underparts, and a pale supercilium. It is found in grasslands of southern South America.

children.name: Geospizopsis
children.description: A genus of plain-coloured finches found in the high Andes of South America, with grey or brown plumage and conical bills.

children.name: Geospizopsis plumbea
children.description: A finch with lead-grey plumage, a black bill, and white outer tail feathers. It is found in the high Andes of Peru and Bolivia.

children.name: Phrygilus
children.description: A genus of finches with grey, black, and white plumage, found in the high Andes of South America. They inhabit rocky slopes and dry scrub at high elevations.

children.name: Phrygilus gayi
children.description:
The grey-hooded sierra finch (Phrygilus gayi) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae.
It is found in Argentina and Chile where its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical dry shrubland and subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland.

children.name: Phrygilus punensis
children.description:
The Peruvian sierra finch (Phrygilus punensis) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae.
It is found in western Bolivia and Peru where its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical high-altitude shrubland.

children.name: Phrygilus atacamensis
children.description: A finch with a grey head, yellow underparts, and brown back. It is found in the arid highlands of Chile and Argentina.

children.name: Phrygilus patagonicus
children.description:
The Patagonian sierra finch (Phrygilus patagonicus) is a species of bird in the family Thraupidae. It is found in Argentina and Chile.
Its natural habitats are temperate forests, subtropical or tropical dry shrubland, and temperate grassland.

children.name: Oryzoborus
children.description: A genus of finches with massive, thick bills adapted for cracking hard seeds, found in wet lowlands of Central and South America. They are sometimes placed in the tanager family but are now considered New World sparrows.

children.name: Sporophila
children.description: A large genus of small, seed-eating finches with thick conical bills, found across Central and South America. Males often have striking black, white, and chestnut plumage patterns, while females are drab brown. Many species are popular cage birds.

children.name: Sporophila muralata
children.description: A small seedeater with black and white plumage, found in grasslands of southeastern Colombia.

children.name: Sporophila nigra
children.description: A seedeater with completely black plumage in males, brown in females. It is endemic to the Antilles.

children.name: Sporophila albicauda
children.description: A seedeater with a black head, white tail, grey back, and white underparts. It is found in grasslands of central South America.

children.name: Sporophila cinerea
children.description: A seedeater with grey upperparts, white underparts, and a stout grey bill. It is found in grasslands of South America.

children.name: Sporophila melanocephala
children.description: A seedeater with a black head, rufous breast, grey back, and white belly. It is found in grasslands of southern South America.

children.name: Sporophila pilzei
children.description: A seedeater with a black head and breast, grey back, and white belly. It is endemic to the Cerrado region of Brazil.
